Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are TallWave's redlines to the Order Form and a short comment sheet from procurement highlighting three items that need clarity before legal signs:
- Minimum commit phasing (we prefer quarterly tranches with a 60-day notice rather than a single annual commit).
- Net terms: finance is pushing Net45 across vendors — can you confirm Redwood's flexibility and whether there are any fees for Net45?
- Tax treatment: TallWave is an EU-headquartered entity using reverse-charge for VAT in a number of contracts — procurement needs the ordering party / remit entity to be explicit.

We also attached a clean copy of the redline (TallWave_Redlines_v1.pdf) and a short pricing spreadsheet with the proposed staging (pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx). Can Kimberly or your legal team take a look and flag anything that will block our PO?

We need to get to signature by end of month to hit our Q3 launch. If there are commercial concessions needed (prepay, holdback, or activation-fee changes) please let us know options and timelines.

Best,
Ava Reynolds
Head of Procurement, TallWave

Ava — thanks for the redlines and the clear list. Summary response below; please see inline notes in our clean Order Form (RW_OrderForm_v2_clean.pdf) attached.

Quick summary of what we can do and what we need to escalate:
1) Minimum commit phasing — we can accept quarterly tranches (split into four equal tranches) but we need the contract to include a fixed tranche schedule (dates + amounts) rather than an open 60-day notice to avoid unbounded exposure. I put a suggested tranche table in the clean copy.
2) Net terms — Finance: Redwood generally runs Net30. We can offer Net45 as a concession for enterprise accounts but require either (a) a 15% prepay on the first tranche, OR (b) a short-term credit line (billing holdback) secured by purchase order numbering. Ben, Kimberly — does Finance/legal want to weigh in on which concession is easier operationally?
3) Tax / remit entity — we need TallWave to confirm remit entity on the PO. For EU reverse-charge we can add explicit invoice remarks and a VAT clause referencing reverse-charge, but we cannot change the billing entity on our side without approval from Revenue. Kimberly — I flagged the VAT language for legal review.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly to review the contractual language for gross-up / reverse charge (target EOD today).
- Ben to confirm whether Sales is okay with a 15% prepay vs billing holdback (ask: which is marketable to the customer).
- TallWave to confirm which legal entity will appear on the PO and whether their AP can accept split invoices per tranche.

If we can get agreement on the prepay or holdback today, we can move straight to final signature routing.

Thanks — Tessa

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Attachments: RW_OrderForm_v2_clean.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: TallWave redlines + tax question on order form

Tessa / Ben / TallWave — quick legal notes after a first pass through the redline:

1) Minimum commit phrasing: don't accept open-ended 60-day decommit language. Add a specific tranche schedule (dates + amounts) and a one-time opportunity for TallWave to reallocate up to 20% of a tranche in writing 30 days before invoice. That preserves predictability for capacity planning.

2) Net terms: legal is OK operationally with Net45 provided:
   - we include a 1.5% monthly late fee after term (capped at 12%).
   - TallWave provides a PO referencing deal ID DL-4892 for each tranche invoice.
   - We include a clause requiring AP contact and remit entity on the first PO; absent that, Redwood invoices the Redwood US entity and TallWave self-reports VAT as applicable.

3) VAT / reverse-charge: we will add an invoice footnote referencing EU reverse-charge and require TallWave to confirm VAT registration number at countersign. We will not take responsibility for third-country withholding without explicit gross-up language. If TallWave requires gross-up for any withholding, this must be a negotiated commercial concession (we will need to price that in).

4) Activation/proration: propose that activation fees for partially used tranches are prorated by days in the first tranche only; after the first tranche, fees are non-refundable.

I made inline redlines in RW_OrderForm_v2_clean.pdf and added language suggestions. If TallWave can accept the tranche table and PO requirements we can cut a signature copy this week.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachments: RW_OrderForm_v2_clean.pdf (legal-redlines, 2 pages)

Looping in my quick commercial call: I'm OK to approve Net45 for the contract on the condition of option (a) 15% prepay on tranche 1 OR option (b) PO-backed billing holdback (Finance to implement). My preference is prepay — cleaner for renewal conversations and lower ledger risk. If TallWave pushes back on prepay, we can offer a one-time credit facility but we'll need finance to run the underwriting (this will add 5 business days).

Tessa — please present the tranche schedule and the 15% prepay ask to Ava this morning. If TallWave confirms entity remit and PO cadence I want this to signature-ready by Tuesday EOD.

Ben Carter
